commemorations.local: Sixth Day Within the Octave of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

verses.text: In die illa cantábitur cánticum istud in terra Juda: Urbs fortitúdinis nostræ Sion Salvátor, ponétur in ea murus et antemurále.
Aperíte portas et ingrediátur gens justa, custódiens veritátem.
Vetus error ábiit: servábis pacem: pacem, quia in te sperávimus.

responsory.text: Ecce apparébit Dóminus super nubem cándidam,
responsory.repeat: Et cum eo Sanctórum míllia: et habébit in vestiménto, et in fémore suo scriptum: Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium.

responsory.text: Apparébit in finem, et non mentiétur; si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniens véniet.
Et cum eo Sanctórum míllia: et habébit in vestiménto, et in fémore suo scriptum: Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium.

parts.title: Lesson from the book of Isaias

verses.text: In that day shall this canticle be sung in the land of Juda. Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein.
Open ye the gates, and let the just nation, that keepeth the truth, enter in.
The old error is passed away: thou wilt keep peace: peace, because we have hoped in thee.

responsory.text: Behold, the Lord shall appear upon a white cloud,
responsory.repeat: And ten thousand of His saints with Him; and He shall have on His vesture, and on His thigh a name written King of kings, and Lord of lords.

responsory.text: He shall appear and not lie; though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will surely come.
And ten thousand of His saints with Him; and He shall have on His vesture, and on His thigh a name written King of kings, and Lord of lords.

verses.text: Sperástis in Dómino in sǽculis ætérnis, in Dómino Deo forti, in perpétuum.
Quia incurvábit habitántes in excélso, civitátem sublímem humiliábit. Humiliábit eam usque ad terram, détrahet eam usque ad púlverem.
Conculcábit eam pes, pedes páuperis, gressus egenórum.

responsory.text: Béthlehem cívitas Dei summi, ex te éxiet Dominátor Israël, et egréssus ejus sicut a princípio diérum æternitátis, et magnificábitur in médio univérsæ terræ:
responsory.repeat: Et pax erit in terra nostra, dum vénerit.

responsory.text: Loquétur pacem in géntibus, et potéstas ejus a mari usque ad mare.
Et pax erit in terra nostra, dum vénerit.

verses.text: You have hoped in the Lord for evermore, in the Lord God mighty for ever.
For he shall bring down them that dwell on high, the high city he shall lay low. He shall bring it down even to the ground, he shall pull it down even to the dust.
The foot shall tread it down, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy.

responsory.text: Thou, Bethlehem, art the city of the Most High God, out of thee shall He come forth That is to be Ruler in Israel; Whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting, and now shall He be great unto the ends of the earth.
responsory.repeat: And this Man shall be the peace in our land, when He shall come.

responsory.text: He shall speak peace unto the Gentiles, and shall have dominion from sea to sea.
And this Man shall be the peace in our land, when He shall come.

verses.text: Sémita justi recta est, rectus callis justi ad ambulándum.
Et in sémita judiciórum tuórum, Dómine, sustinúimus te: nomen tuum, et memoriále tuum in desidério ánimæ.
Anima mea desiderávit te in nocte, sed et spíritu meo in præcórdiis meis de mane vigilábo ad te. Cum féceris judícia tua in terra, justítiam discent habitatóres orbis.
Misereámur ímpio, et non discet justítiam: in terra sanctórum iníqua gessit, et non vidébit glóriam Dómini.

responsory.text: Qui ventúrus est, véniet, et non tardábit: et jam non erit timor in fínibus nostris:
responsory.repeat: Quóniam ipse est Salvátor noster.

responsory.text: Depónet omnes iniquitátes nostras, et proíciet in profúndum maris ómnia peccáta nostra.
Quóniam ipse est Salvátor noster.

verses.text: The way of the just is right, the path of the just is right to walk in.
And in the way of thy judgments, O Lord, we have patiently waited for thee: thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul.

My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me in the morning early I will watch to thee. When thou shalt do thy judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn justice.
Let us have pity on the wicked, but he will not learn justice: in the land of the saints he hath done wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.

responsory.text: He That shall come, will come, and will not tarry; and there shall no more be fear in our borders.
responsory.repeat: For He is our Saviour.

responsory.text: He shall tread down all our iniquities, and cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.
For He is our Saviour.

verses.text: Dómine, exaltétur manus tua, et non vídeant: vídeant, et confundántur zelántes pópuli: et ignis hostes tuos dévoret.
Dómine, dabis pacem nobis: ómnia enim ópera nostra operátus es nobis.
Dómine Deus noster, possedérunt nos dómini absque te, tantum in te recordémur nóminis tui.
Moriéntes non vivant, gigántes non resúrgant: proptérea visitásti et contrivísti eos, et perdidísti omnem memóriam eórum.

responsory.text: Ecce véniet Dóminus princeps regum terræ;
responsory.repeat: Beáti qui paráti sunt occúrrere illi, † habébunt partem in civitáte Jerúsalem.

responsory.text: Veniens veniet Dominus, et non tardabit.
Beáti qui paráti sunt occúrrere illi, † habébunt partem in civitáte Jerúsalem.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Beáti qui paráti sunt occúrrere illi, † habébunt partem in civitáte Jerúsalem.

verses.text: Lord, let thy hand be exalted, and let them not see: let the envious people see, and be confounded: and let fire devour thy enemies.
Lord, thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us.
O Lord our God, other lords besides thee have had dominion over us, only in thee let us remember thy name.
Let not the dead live, let not the giants rise again: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and hast destroyed all their memory.

responsory.text: Behold the Lord, the Prince of the kings of the earth, shall come,
responsory.repeat: Blessed are they who are ready to meet him, they shall have their portion in the city of Jerusalem.

responsory.text: The Lord will surely come and will not tarry.
Blessed are they who are ready to meet him, they shall have their portion in the city of Jerusalem.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Blessed are they who are ready to meet him, they shall have their portion in the city of Jerusalem.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Leónis Papæ
parts.source: Sermo 2 de jejúnio décimi mensis et collectis
paragraphs: Quod témporis rátio, et devotiónis nostræ ádmonet consuetúdo, pastoráli vobis, dilectíssimi, sollicitúdine prædicámus, décimi mensis celebrándum esse jejúnium, quo pro consummáta perceptióne ómnium frúctuum, digníssime largitóri eórum Deo continéntiæ libámen offértur.

responsory.text: Ægýpte, noli flere, quia Dominátor tuus véniet tibi, ante cujus conspéctum movebúntur abýssi,
responsory.repeat: Liberáre pópulum suum de manu poténtiæ.

responsory.text: Ecce véniet Dóminus exercítuum, Deus tuus cum potestáte magna.
Liberáre pópulum suum de manu poténtiæ.

parts.title: From the Sermons of Pope St. Leo (the Great)
parts.source: Second on the December Fast, and Almsgiving
paragraphs: Dearly beloved brethren, with the care which becometh us as the shepherd of your souls, we urge upon you the rigid observance of this December Fast. The month of December hath come round again, and with it this devout custom of the Church. The fruits of the year, which is drawing to a close, are now all gathered in, and we most meetly offer our abstinence to God as a sacrifice of thanksgiving.

responsory.text: Weep not, O Egypt, for the Ruler cometh unto thee, and the depths shall be moved at His presence.
responsory.repeat: To deliver His people out of the hand of the mighty.

responsory.text: Behold, the Lord of hosts, thy God, cometh with great power.
To deliver His people out of the hand of the mighty.

paragraphs: Quid enim potest efficácius esse jejúnio? cujus observántia appropinquámus Deo, et resisténtes diábolo, vítia blanda superámus. Semper enim virtúti cibus jejúnium fuit. De abstinéntia dénique pródeunt castæ cogitatiónes, rationábiles voluntátes, salubrióra consília: et per voluntárias afflictiónes caro concupiscéntiis móritur, virtútibus spíritus innovátur.

responsory.text: Prope est ut véniat tempus ejus, et dies ejus non elongabúntur:
responsory.repeat: Miserébitur Dóminus Jacob, et Israël salvábitur.

responsory.text: Revértere, virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas.
Miserébitur Dóminus Jacob, et Israël salvábitur.

paragraphs: And what can be more useful than fasting, that exercise by which we draw nigh to God, make a stand against the devil, and overcome the softer enticements of sin? Fasting hath ever been the bread of strength. From abstinence proceed pure thoughts, reasonable desires, and healthy counsels. By voluntary mortifications the flesh dieth to lust, and the soul is renewed in might.

responsory.text: Her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.
responsory.repeat: Lord shall have mercy on Jacob, and Israel shall be saved.

responsory.text: Turn again, O Virgin of Israel, turn again to thy cities.
For the Lord shall have mercy on Judah, and Israel shall be saved.

paragraphs: Sed quia non solo jejúnio animárum nostrárum salus acquíritur, jejúnium nostrum misericórdiis páuperum suppleámus. Impendámus virtúti, quod subtráhimus voluptáti. Fiat reféctio páuperis abstinéntia jejunántis. Studeámus viduárum defensióni, pupillórum utilitáti, lugéntium consolatióni, dissidéntium paci. Suscipiátur peregrínus, adjuvétur oppréssus, vestiátur nudus, foveátur ægrótus: ut quicúmque nostrum de justis labóribus auctóri bonórum ómnium Deo sacrifícium hujus pietátis obtúlerit, ab eodem regni cæléstis prǽmium percípere mereátur.

responsory.text: Descéndet Dóminus sicut plúvia in vellus:
responsory.repeat: Oriétur in diébus ejus justítia, et abundántia pacis.

responsory.text: Et adorábunt eum omnes reges, omnes gentes sérvient ei.
Oriétur in diébus ejus justítia, et abundántia pacis.

paragraphs: But since fasting is not the only mean whereby we get health for our souls, let us add to our fasting works of mercy. Let us spend in good deeds what we take from indulgence. Let our fast become the banquet of the poor. Let us defend the widow and serve the orphan; let us comfort the afflicted and reconcile the estranged; let us take in the wanderer and succour the oppressed; let us clothe the naked and cherish the sick. And may every one of us that shall offer to the God of all goodness this Advent sacrifice of fasting and alms be by Him fitted to receive an eternal reward in His heavenly kingdom!

responsory.text: The Lord shall come down like rain upon a fleece.
responsory.repeat: In His days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace.

responsory.text: All the kings of the earth shall fall down before Him, all nations shall serve Him.
In His days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace.

paragraphs: Quarta ígitur et sexta Feria jejunémus; Sábbato autem apud beátum Petrum Apóstolum páriter vigilémus: cujus suffragántibus méritis, quæ póscimus, impetráre possímus per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

responsory.text: Egrediétur virga de radíce Jesse, et flos de radíce ejus ascendet:
responsory.repeat: Et erit justítia cíngulum lumbórum ejus, † et fides cinctórium renum ejus.

responsory.text: Et requiéscet super eum spíritus Dómini: † spíritus sapiéntiæ, et intelléctus: spíritus consílii, et fortitúdinis.
Et erit justítia cíngulum lumbórum ejus, † et fides cinctórium renum ejus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Et erit justítia cíngulum lumbórum ejus, † et fides cinctórium renum ejus.

paragraphs: We fast on Wednesday and Friday; and there is likewise a Vigil on Saturday at the Church of St. Peter, that by his good prayers we may the more effectually obtain what we ask for, through our Lord Jesus Christ, Who with the Father and the Holy Ghost, liveth and reigneth, God, world without end. Amen.

responsory.text: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse and a branch shall grow out of his roots.
responsory.repeat: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

responsory.text: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.
And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Joánnem
paragraphs: In illo tempore: Misérunt Judǽi ab Jerosólymis sacerdótes et levítas ad Joánnem, ut interrogárent eum: Tu quis es? Et conféssus est, et non negávit: et conféssus est: Quia non sum ego Christus. Et interrogavérunt eum: Quid ergo? Elías es tu? Et dixit: Non sum. Prophéta es tu? Et respondit: Non. Dixérunt ergo ei: Quis es, ut respónsum demus his, qui misérunt nos? Quid dicis de te ipso? Ait: Ego vox clamántis in desérto: Dirígite viam Dómini, sicut dixit Isaías Prophéta. Et qui missi fúerant, erant ex pharisǽis. Et interrogavérunt eum, et dixérunt ei: Quid ergo baptízas, si tu non es Christus, neque Elías, neque Prophéta? Respóndit eis Joánnes, dicens: Ego baptízo in aqua: médius autem vestrum stetit, quem vos nescítis. Ipse est, qui post me ventúrus est, qui ante me factus est: cujus ego non sum dignus ut solvam ejus corrígiam calceaménti. Hæc in Bethánia facta sunt trans Jordánem, ubi erat Joánnes baptízans.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ
paragraphs: Ex hujus nobis lectiónis verbis, fratres caríssimi, Joánnis humílitas commendátur: qui cum tantæ virtútis esset, ut Christus credi potuísset, elégit sólide subsístere in se, ne humána opinióne raperétur inániter super se. Nam conféssus est, et non negávit: et conféssus est, Quia non sum ego Christus. Sed qui dixit, Non sum; negávit plane quod non erat, sed non negávit quod erat: ut veritátem loquens, ejus membrum fíeret, cujus sibi nomen falláciter non usurpáret.

responsory.text: Veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre: reláxa facínora plebi tuæ,
responsory.repeat: Et révoca dispérsos in terram suam.

responsory.text: Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni, ut salvos fácias nos.
Et révoca dispérsos in terram suam.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to John
paragraphs: In that time were sent from Jerusalem priests and Levites to John, to ask him: Who art thou? ? And he confessed and did not deny: and he confessed: I am not the Christ. And they asked him: What then? Art thou Elias? And he said: I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered: No. They said therefore unto him: Who art thou, that we may give an answer to them that sent us? What sayest thou of thyself? He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias. And they that were sent were of the Pharisees. And they asked him and said to him: Why then dost thou baptize, if thou be not Christ, nor Elias, nor the prophet? John answered them, saying: I baptize with water: but there hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not. The same is he that shall come after me, who is preferred before me: the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose. These things were done in Bethania, beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

parts.title: Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great)
paragraphs: Dearly beloved brethren, the first thing which striketh us in today's Gospel is the lowly-mindedness of John. He was so great that it was thought he might be the Christ; yet he soberly chose rather to seem only what he really was, than to let the belief of men invest him with a dignity which did not belong to him; for he confessed, and denied not, but confessed, I am not the Christ, at the same time he would not deny what he was in reality; and thus his very truth-speaking made him a member of Him Whose title he would not by falsehood take.

responsory.text: O Lord, come and make no tarrying; loosen the bonds of thy people.
responsory.repeat: And gather again into their own land them that are scattered abroad.

responsory.text: O Lord, stir up thy strength, and come and save us.
And gather again into their own land them that are scattered abroad.

paragraphs: Cum ergo non vult appétere nomen Christi, factus est membrum Christi: quia dum infirmitátem suam stúduit humíliter agnóscere, illíus celsitúdinem méruit veráciter obtinére. Sed cum ex lectióne alia, Redemptóris nostri senténtia ad mentem redúcitur, ex hujus lectiónis verbis nobis quǽstio valde impléxa generátur. Alio quippe in loco inquisítus a discípulis Dóminus de Elíæ advéntu, respóndit: Elías jam venit, et non cognovérunt eum, sed fecérunt in eum quæcúmque voluérunt: et, si vultis scire, Joánnes ipse est Elías.

responsory.text: Ecce radix Jesse descéndet in salútem populórum, ipsum gentes deprecabúntur:
responsory.repeat: Et erit nomen ejus gloriósum.

responsory.text: Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum.
Et erit nomen ejus gloriósum.

paragraphs: In that he arrogated not to himself the name of Christ, he became a member of Christ. While he humbly strove to confess his own weakness, he earned by his simplicity a part in the grandeur of his Master.

In considering this subject we find an apparent contradiction between one of John's statements, and the saying of our Redeemer recorded in another part of the Gospel. (Matth. xvii. 10-12.) When His disciples asked our Lord regarding the coming of Elias, He answered: Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. And if ye will receive it, this (that is, John) is Elias. (Matth. xi. 14.)

responsory.text: Behold, there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall come for salvation unto the people, to it shall the Gentiles seek;
responsory.repeat: And His name shall be glorious.

responsory.text: The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.
And His name shall be glorious.

paragraphs: Requisítus autem Joánnes dicit: Non sum Elías. Quid est hoc, fratres caríssimi, quia quod Véritas affírmat, hoc prophéta Veritátis negat? Valde namque inter se divérsa sunt: Ipse est: et, Non sum. Quómodo ergo prophéta veritátis est, si ejusdem Veritátis sermónibus concors non est? Sed si subtíliter véritas ipsa requirátur, hoc quod inter se contrárium sonat, quómodo contrárium non sit, invenítur.

responsory.text: Docébit nos Dóminus vias suas, et ambulábimus in sémitis ejus:
responsory.repeat: Quia de Sion exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.

responsory.text: Veníte, ascendámus ad montem Dómini, et ad domum Dei Jacob.
Quia de Sion exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.

paragraphs: But when John was asked if he was Elias, he answered: I am not. How comes it then, dearly beloved brethren, that we find the Truth Itself asserting what the prophet of the Truth denied? It must evidently be that our Lord meant one thing and John another, when the Lord said, This is, and John, I am not. For how can he be the prophet of truth, if he speak not according to the word of Him Who is the Eternal Truth? Let us then more minutely examine these words, and we shall find that there is no real contradiction.

responsory.text: The Lord will teach us of His ways, and we will walk in His paths.
responsory.repeat: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

responsory.text: Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob.
For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

paragraphs: Ad Zacharíam namque de Joánne Angelus dicit: Ipse præcédet ante illum in spíritu et virtúte Elíæ. Qui idcírco ventúrus in spíritu et virtúte Elíæ dícitur, quia sicut Elías secúndum Dómini advéntum prævéniet, ita Joánnes prævénit primum. Sicut ille præcúrsor ventúrus est Júdicis, ita iste præcúrsor est factus Redemptóris. Joánnes ígitur in spíritu Elías erat, in persóna Elías non erat. Quod ergo Dóminus fatétur de spíritu, hoc Joánnes dénegat de persóna.

responsory.text: Súscipe verbum, Virgo María, quod tibi a Dómino per Angelum transmíssum est: concípies et páries Deum páriter et hóminem,
responsory.repeat: Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.

responsory.text: Páries quidem fílium, et virginitátis non patiéris detriméntum: efficiéris grávida, et eris mater semper intácta.
Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.

paragraphs: When the Angel announced to Zacharias the coming birth of John he said He shall go before Him in the spirit and power of Elias, (Luke i. 17.) As the old Elias will come again before the Second Advent of the Lord, so did John, as the new Elias, go before the First Advent, in the spirit and power of Elias. As the old Elias will be the Fore-runner of the Judge, so the new Elias was the Forerunner of the Saviour. John then was Elias in spirit, but not in person; and our Lord asserteth of the spirit what John denieth of the person.

responsory.text: Receive, O Virgin Mary, receive the word of the Lord, which is sent thee by His Angel; thou shalt conceive, and shalt bring forth God and Man together.
responsory.repeat: And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.

responsory.text: Thou shalt bring forth a son, and remain a maiden undefiled thou shalt conceive and be a Mother, still Virgin unspotted.
And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.

Matins · Sunday, 13 December 2026

Third Sunday of Advent

Dominica III Adventus · Semiduplex II classis

Commemorations: St. Lucy, Virgin and Martyr; Sixth Day Within the Octave of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

Lesson from the book of Isaias

Isa 26:1-3

In that day shall this canticle be sung in the land of Juda. Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein. Open ye the gates, and let the just nation, that keepeth the truth, enter in. The old error is passed away: thou wilt keep peace: peace, because we have hoped in thee.

℟. Behold, the Lord shall appear upon a white cloud, * And ten thousand of His saints with Him; and He shall have on His vesture, and on His thigh a name written King of kings, and Lord of lords.

℣. He shall appear and not lie; though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will surely come.

℟. And ten thousand of His saints with Him; and He shall have on His vesture, and on His thigh a name written King of kings, and Lord of lords.

Lesson II

Isa 26:4-6

You have hoped in the Lord for evermore, in the Lord God mighty for ever. For he shall bring down them that dwell on high, the high city he shall lay low. He shall bring it down even to the ground, he shall pull it down even to the dust. The foot shall tread it down, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy.

℟. Thou, Bethlehem, art the city of the Most High God, out of thee shall He come forth That is to be Ruler in Israel; Whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting, and now shall He be great unto the ends of the earth. * And this Man shall be the peace in our land, when He shall come.

℣. He shall speak peace unto the Gentiles, and shall have dominion from sea to sea.

℟. And this Man shall be the peace in our land, when He shall come.

Lesson III

Isa 26:7-10

The way of the just is right, the path of the just is right to walk in. And in the way of thy judgments, O Lord, we have patiently waited for thee: thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul. My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me in the morning early I will watch to thee. When thou shalt do thy judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn justice. Let us have pity on the wicked, but he will not learn justice: in the land of the saints he hath done wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.

℟. He That shall come, will come, and will not tarry; and there shall no more be fear in our borders. * For He is our Saviour.

℣. He shall tread down all our iniquities, and cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.

℟. For He is our Saviour.

Lesson IV

Isa 26:11-14

Lord, let thy hand be exalted, and let them not see: let the envious people see, and be confounded: and let fire devour thy enemies. ℟. And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.

Lesson from the book of Isaias

Isa 26:1-3

Isa 26:1-3

Dearly beloved brethren, with the care which becometh us as the shepherd of your souls, we urge upon you the rigid observance of this December Fast. The month of December hath come round again, and with it this devout custom of the Church. The fruits of the year, which is drawing to a close, are now all gathered in, and we most meetly offer our abstinence to God as a sacrifice of thanksgiving.

℟. Ægýpte, noli flere, quia Dominátor tuus véniet tibi, ante cujus conspéctum movebúntur abýssi, * Liberáre pópulum suum de manu poténtiæ.

℟. Weep not, O Egypt, for the Ruler cometh unto thee, and the depths shall be moved at His presence. * To deliver His people out of the hand of the mighty.

℣. Ecce véniet Dóminus exercítuum, Deus tuus cum potestáte magna.

℣. Behold, the Lord of hosts, thy God, cometh with great power.

℟. Liberáre pópulum suum de manu poténtiæ.

℟. To deliver His people out of the hand of the mighty.

Lectio VI

Lesson VI

Quid enim potest efficácius esse jejúnio? cujus observántia appropinquámus Deo, et resisténtes diábolo, vítia blanda superámus. Semper enim virtúti cibus jejúnium fuit. De abstinéntia dénique pródeunt castæ cogitatiónes, rationábiles voluntátes, salubrióra consília: et per voluntárias afflictiónes caro concupiscéntiis móritur, virtútibus spíritus innovátur.

And what can be more useful than fasting, that exercise by which we draw nigh to God, make a stand against the devil, and overcome the softer enticements of sin? Fasting hath ever been the bread of strength. From abstinence proceed pure thoughts, reasonable desires, and healthy counsels. By voluntary mortifications the flesh dieth to lust, and the soul is renewed in might.

℟. Prope est ut véniat tempus ejus, et dies ejus non elongabúntur: * Miserébitur Dóminus Jacob, et Israël salvábitur.

℟. Her time is near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged. * Lord shall have mercy on Jacob, and Israel shall be saved.

℣. Revértere, virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas.

℣. Turn again, O Virgin of Israel, turn again to thy cities.

℟. Miserébitur Dóminus Jacob, et Israël salvábitur.

℟. For the Lord shall have mercy on Judah, and Israel shall be saved.

Lectio VII

Lesson VII

Sed quia non solo jejúnio animárum nostrárum salus acquíritur, jejúnium nostrum misericórdiis páuperum suppleámus. Impendámus virtúti, quod subtráhimus voluptáti. Fiat reféctio páuperis abstinéntia jejunántis. Studeámus viduárum defensióni, pupillórum utilitáti, lugéntium consolatióni, dissidéntium paci. Suscipiátur peregrínus, adjuvétur oppréssus, vestiátur nudus, foveátur ægrótus: ut quicúmque nostrum de justis labóribus auctóri bonórum ómnium Deo sacrifícium hujus pietátis obtúlerit, ab eodem regni cæléstis prǽmium percípere mereátur.

But since fasting is not the only mean whereby we get health for our souls, let us add to our fasting works of mercy. Let us spend in good deeds what we take from indulgence. Let our fast become the banquet of the poor. Let us defend the widow and serve the orphan; let us comfort the afflicted and reconcile the estranged; let us take in the wanderer and succour the oppressed; let us clothe the naked and cherish the sick. And may every one of us that shall offer to the God of all goodness this Advent sacrifice of fasting and alms be by Him fitted to receive an eternal reward in His heavenly kingdom!

℟. Descéndet Dóminus sicut plúvia in vellus: * Oriétur in diébus ejus justítia, et abundántia pacis.

℟. The Lord shall come down like rain upon a fleece. * In His days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace.

℣. Et adorábunt eum omnes reges, omnes gentes sérvient ei.

℣. All the kings of the earth shall fall down before Him, all nations shall serve Him.

℟. Oriétur in diébus ejus justítia, et abundántia pacis.

℟. In His days shall righteousness flourish, and abundance of peace.

Lectio VIII

Lesson VIII

Quarta ígitur et sexta Feria jejunémus; Sábbato autem apud beátum Petrum Apóstolum páriter vigilémus: cujus suffragántibus méritis, quæ póscimus, impetráre possímus per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

We fast on Wednesday and Friday; and there is likewise a Vigil on Saturday at the Church of St. Peter, that by his good prayers we may the more effectually obtain what we ask for, through our Lord Jesus Christ, Who with the Father and the Holy Ghost, liveth and reigneth, God, world without end. Amen.

℟. Egrediétur virga de radíce Jesse, et flos de radíce ejus ascendet: * Et erit justítia cíngulum lumbórum ejus, † et fides cinctórium renum ejus.

℟. There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse and a branch shall grow out of his roots. * And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

℣. Et requiéscet super eum spíritus Dómini: † spíritus sapiéntiæ, et intelléctus: spíritus consílii, et fortitúdinis.

℣. And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.

℟. Et erit justítia cíngulum lumbórum ejus, † et fides cinctórium renum ejus.

℟. And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Et erit justítia cíngulum lumbórum ejus, † et fides cinctórium renum ejus.

℟. And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

Lectio IX

Lesson IX

Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Joánnem

From the Holy Gospel according to John

Joannes 1:19-28

John 1:19-28

In illo tempore: Misérunt Judǽi ab Jerosólymis sacerdótes et levítas ad Joánnem, ut interrogárent eum: Tu quis es? Et conféssus est, et non negávit: et conféssus est: Quia non sum ego Christus. Et interrogavérunt eum: Quid ergo? Elías es tu? Et dixit: Non sum. Prophéta es tu? Et respondit: Non. Dixérunt ergo ei: Quis es, ut respónsum demus his, qui misérunt nos? Quid dicis de te ipso? Ait: Ego vox clamántis in desérto: Dirígite viam Dómini, sicut dixit Isaías Prophéta. Et qui missi fúerant, erant ex pharisǽis. Et interrogavérunt eum, et dixérunt ei: Quid ergo baptízas, si tu non es Christus, neque Elías, neque Prophéta? Respóndit eis Joánnes, dicens: Ego baptízo in aqua: médius autem vestrum stetit, quem vos nescítis. Ipse est, qui post me ventúrus est, qui ante me factus est: cujus ego non sum dignus ut solvam ejus corrígiam calceaménti. Hæc in Bethánia facta sunt trans Jordánem, ubi erat Joánnes baptízans.

In that time were sent from Jerusalem priests and Levites to John, to ask him: Who art thou? ? And he confessed and did not deny: and he confessed: I am not the Christ. And they asked him: What then? Art thou Elias? And he said: I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered: No. They said therefore unto him: Who art thou, that we may give an answer to them that sent us? What sayest thou of thyself? He said: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias. And they that were sent were of the Pharisees. And they asked him and said to him: Why then dost thou baptize, if thou be not Christ, nor Elias, nor the prophet? John answered them, saying: I baptize with water: but there hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not. The same is he that shall come after me, who is preferred before me: the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose. These things were done in Bethania, beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ

Homily by Pope St. Gregory (the Great)

Homilia 7 in Evangelia

7th on the Gospels

Ex hujus nobis lectiónis verbis, fratres caríssimi, Joánnis humílitas commendátur: qui cum tantæ virtútis esset, ut Christus credi potuísset, elégit sólide subsístere in se, ne humána opinióne raperétur inániter super se. Nam conféssus est, et non negávit: et conféssus est, Quia non sum ego Christus. Sed qui dixit, Non sum; negávit plane quod non erat, sed non negávit quod erat: ut veritátem loquens, ejus membrum fíeret, cujus sibi nomen falláciter non usurpáret.

Dearly beloved brethren, the first thing which striketh us in today's Gospel is the lowly-mindedness of John. He was so great that it was thought he might be the Christ; yet he soberly chose rather to seem only what he really was, than to let the belief of men invest him with a dignity which did not belong to him; for he confessed, and denied not, but confessed, I am not the Christ, at the same time he would not deny what he was in reality; and thus his very truth-speaking made him a member of Him Whose title he would not by falsehood take.

℟. Veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre: reláxa facínora plebi tuæ, * Et révoca dispérsos in terram suam.

℟. O Lord, come and make no tarrying; loosen the bonds of thy people. * And gather again into their own land them that are scattered abroad.

℣. Excita, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni, ut salvos fácias nos.

℣. O Lord, stir up thy strength, and come and save us.

℟. Et révoca dispérsos in terram suam.

℟. And gather again into their own land them that are scattered abroad.

Lectio X

Lesson X

Cum ergo non vult appétere nomen Christi, factus est membrum Christi: quia dum infirmitátem suam stúduit humíliter agnóscere, illíus celsitúdinem méruit veráciter obtinére. Sed cum ex lectióne alia, Redemptóris nostri senténtia ad mentem redúcitur, ex hujus lectiónis verbis nobis quǽstio valde impléxa generátur. Alio quippe in loco inquisítus a discípulis Dóminus de Elíæ advéntu, respóndit: Elías jam venit, et non cognovérunt eum, sed fecérunt in eum quæcúmque voluérunt: et, si vultis scire, Joánnes ipse est Elías.

In that he arrogated not to himself the name of Christ, he became a member of Christ. While he humbly strove to confess his own weakness, he earned by his simplicity a part in the grandeur of his Master.

In considering this subject we find an apparent contradiction between one of John's statements, and the saying of our Redeemer recorded in another part of the Gospel. (Matth. xvii. 10-12.) When His disciples asked our Lord regarding the coming of Elias, He answered: Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. And if ye will receive it, this (that is, John) is Elias. (Matth. xi. 14.)

℟. Ecce radix Jesse descéndet in salútem populórum, ipsum gentes deprecabúntur: * Et erit nomen ejus gloriósum.

℟. Behold, there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall come for salvation unto the people, to it shall the Gentiles seek; * And His name shall be glorious.

℣. Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David, patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum.

℣. The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.

℟. Et erit nomen ejus gloriósum.

℟. And His name shall be glorious.

Lectio XI

Lesson XI

Requisítus autem Joánnes dicit: Non sum Elías. Quid est hoc, fratres caríssimi, quia quod Véritas affírmat, hoc prophéta Veritátis negat? Valde namque inter se divérsa sunt: Ipse est: et, Non sum. Quómodo ergo prophéta veritátis est, si ejusdem Veritátis sermónibus concors non est? Sed si subtíliter véritas ipsa requirátur, hoc quod inter se contrárium sonat, quómodo contrárium non sit, invenítur.

But when John was asked if he was Elias, he answered: I am not. How comes it then, dearly beloved brethren, that we find the Truth Itself asserting what the prophet of the Truth denied? It must evidently be that our Lord meant one thing and John another, when the Lord said, This is, and John, I am not. For how can he be the prophet of truth, if he speak not according to the word of Him Who is the Eternal Truth? Let us then more minutely examine these words, and we shall find that there is no real contradiction.

℟. Docébit nos Dóminus vias suas, et ambulábimus in sémitis ejus: * Quia de Sion exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.

℟. The Lord will teach us of His ways, and we will walk in His paths. * For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

℣. Veníte, ascendámus ad montem Dómini, et ad domum Dei Jacob.

℣. Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob.

℟. Quia de Sion exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.

℟. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

Lectio XII

Lesson XII

Ad Zacharíam namque de Joánne Angelus dicit: Ipse præcédet ante illum in spíritu et virtúte Elíæ. Qui idcírco ventúrus in spíritu et virtúte Elíæ dícitur, quia sicut Elías secúndum Dómini advéntum prævéniet, ita Joánnes prævénit primum. Sicut ille præcúrsor ventúrus est Júdicis, ita iste præcúrsor est factus Redemptóris. Joánnes ígitur in spíritu Elías erat, in persóna Elías non erat. Quod ergo Dóminus fatétur de spíritu, hoc Joánnes dénegat de persóna.

When the Angel announced to Zacharias the coming birth of John he said He shall go before Him in the spirit and power of Elias, (Luke i. 17.) As the old Elias will come again before the Second Advent of the Lord, so did John, as the new Elias, go before the First Advent, in the spirit and power of Elias. As the old Elias will be the Fore-runner of the Judge, so the new Elias was the Forerunner of the Saviour. John then was Elias in spirit, but not in person; and our Lord asserteth of the spirit what John denieth of the person.

℟. Súscipe verbum, Virgo María, quod tibi a Dómino per Angelum transmíssum est: concípies et páries Deum páriter et hóminem, * Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.

℟. Receive, O Virgin Mary, receive the word of the Lord, which is sent thee by His Angel; thou shalt conceive, and shalt bring forth God and Man together. * And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.

℣. Páries quidem fílium, et virginitátis non patiéris detriméntum: efficiéris grávida, et eris mater semper intácta.

℣. Thou shalt bring forth a son, and remain a maiden undefiled thou shalt conceive and be a Mother, still Virgin unspotted.

℟. Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.

℟. And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Ut benedícta dicáris inter omnes mulíeres.

℟. And thou shalt be called blessed among all women.
